name: Negroni Schoggi
method_note: A citrus-and-cocoa gin variation of the Negroni; method adapted from the classic.
steps: Fill a mixing glass with ice.
Add the Elephant Orange & Cocoa gin, Campari and Carpano Antica Formula in the quantities listed.
Stir until thoroughly chilled, then strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Express the orange twist over the glass and add it as garnish.

name: Negroni normal
method_note: Classic Negroni method; the spreadsheet specifies Tanqueray and Carpano.
steps: Fill a mixing glass with ice.
Add Tanqueray London Dry Gin, Campari and Carpano Antica Formula.
Stir until cold, then strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
Express the orange twist over the drink and garnish.

name: Americano
method_note: The spreadsheet lists alternative sweet vermouth brands; use one, not all.
steps: Fill a highball or rocks glass with plenty of ice.
Add Campari and one of the listed sweet red vermouth options.
Top with soda water to fill the glass.
Stir gently and finish with the orange twist.

name: Bitter Giuseppe (Giusti)
method_note: Adapted from the Bitter Giuseppe using the Giusti vermouth specified in the spreadsheet.
steps: Express the lemon twist over a mixing glass.
Add Cynar, Giusti vermouth, lemon juice (no more than the listed amount) and orange bitters.
Add ice and stir until chilled.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass, then garnish with the lemon twist.

name: Gran Campericano
method_note: House variation; build technique adapted from an Americano. No exact published recipe was located.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the Gran Classico and Campari in the listed amounts.
Add the Indian tonic gently and briefly stir to combine without losing its fizz.
Express the orange twist over the drink and add it.

name: Select Soda
method_note: House variation; technique adapted from the Select Americano, omitting vermouth as in your spreadsheet.
steps: Fill a highball glass with plenty of ice.
Add Select in the range listed (6–9 cl).
Fill the glass with chilled soda water and gently stir.
Finish with an orange twist.

name: Amaretti
method_note: House variation. A stirred amaretto-and-vermouth template was used; no exact published match verified.
steps: Fill a mixing glass with ice.
Measure in Giusti vermouth, Disaronno and the specified drops of orange bitters.
Stir until well chilled.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.

name: Limoncello Spritz normal
method_note: Uses classic limoncello spritz technique, preserving your recipe’s ratios.
steps: Fill a large wine glass with plenty of ice.
Add the limoncello, then gently pour in the chilled prosecco.
Top with soda water and give one gentle stir.
Express and add the lemon twist; serve immediately.

name: Limoncello Spritz Jonas
method_note: Jonas variant retains its different prosecco/limoncello/soda ratio.
steps: Fill a large wine glass with plenty of ice.
Measure the limoncello according to the Jonas version.
Add the prosecco and soda water in the amounts shown and stir very gently.
Finish with a lemon twist and serve.

name: Select Spritz
method_note: The official Select Spritz preparation uses prosecco, Select and soda with an olive garnish.
steps: Fill a large wine glass with plenty of ice.
Add chilled prosecco, Select and soda water in the listed amounts.
Stir briefly and gently to retain carbonation.
Garnish with the pickled olive.

name: Apérol Spritz
method_note: Classic spritz technique; the exact quantities are those in the spreadsheet.
steps: Fill a large wine glass with ice.
Add chilled prosecco, Apérol and soda water.
Gently stir to combine without flattening the bubbles.
Express the orange twist over the drink and garnish.

name: Gran Classico Spritz
method_note: House variation using the standard spritz method; the bitter aperitif is Gran Classico.
steps: Fill a large wine glass with plenty of ice.
Add prosecco, Tempus Fugit Gran Classico and soda water using the listed quantities.
Stir once or twice very gently.
Garnish with the orange twist and serve while sparkling.

name: Gin & Tonic Pfeffer
method_note: Gin and tonic technique; the pink-pepper tonic is the designated mixer.
steps: Fill a highball or balloon glass with the listed amount of ice.
Pour in Hendrick’s gin.
Top gently with Schweppes Pink Pepper Tonic.
Give a short stir and add the cucumber slice(s).

name: Gin & Tonic Seventh Sense
method_note: Gin and tonic technique with the exact branded pairing from the spreadsheet.
steps: Fill a highball glass with the listed amount of ice.
Measure in Seventh Sense gin.
Slowly pour in Swiss Mountain Spring Provençale Tonic.
Stir gently once; no additional garnish is specified in the original recipe.

name: Gin & Tonic Salbei
method_note: The name mentions sage (Salbei), but sage is NOT listed among the original ingredients. None has been added.
steps: Fill a highball glass with the listed amount of ice.
Add Engine gin and top with Tribute tonic.
Gently stir once to combine.
Serve as written; the source spreadsheet specifies no sage or other garnish.

name: Basil Smash
method_note: The muddle-and-shake technique follows published Gin Basil Smash recipes.
steps: Place the basil leaves in a cocktail shaker and muddle gently to release their aroma.
Add Tanqueray gin, sugar syrup and lemon juice in the listed amounts.
Add ice and shake until thoroughly cold.
Double-strain into a rocks glass with fresh ice.

name: Mojito
method_note: Uses the classic muddled mint, lime and sugar approach with the original quantities.
steps: Place the lime pieces, brown sugar and mint in a highball glass.
Muddle gently to extract lime juice and release the mint aroma.
Add white rum and plenty of ice.
Top with soda water to fill the glass and lift gently with a bar spoon.

name: Pimm's
method_note: Your Pimm’s uses ginger beer instead of the more usual ginger ale; retained as written.
steps: Fill a large highball glass with ice.
Add Pimm’s, then the ginger beer in the listed amounts.
Add whatever prepared fruit pieces you have, as noted in the spreadsheet.
Stir gently and finish with the mint leaves.

name: Kyiv Mule
method_note: House mule variant with chili ginger beer and mint; technique follows a Moscow Mule.
steps: Fill a mule mug or highball glass with the listed amount of ice.
Add vodka and freshly squeezed lime juice.
Slowly top with Schweppes Ginger Beer & Chili, stirring lightly.
Finish with the mint leaves.

name: Dry Martini
method_note: The spreadsheet includes a splash of lemon juice, unlike most classic dry martinis; retained as written.
steps: Chill a martini or coupe glass.
Add gin, dry vermouth and the spreadsheet’s splash of lemon juice to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir until thoroughly chilled and strain into the cold glass.
Garnish with the green olive.

name: Hugo
method_note: Hugo method adapted from an elderflower spritz, with syrup instead of elderflower liqueur.
steps: Gently press the mint leaves in a large wine glass with the elderflower syrup.
Add chilled prosecco and soda water in the listed quantities.
Stir briefly and gently; add the lime wedge.
Serve immediately. No ice was specified in the spreadsheet, so it is not added to the ingredient list.

name: Whiskey Sour
method_note: With optional egg white, use a dry shake before shaking with ice.
steps: Measure whiskey, lemon juice, sugar syrup and (if using) egg white into a shaker.
If using egg white, shake vigorously without ice first to create foam.
Add ice and shake until chilled. If omitting egg white, shake once with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass with fresh ice.
